missing_duplicates.description: Completeness check: missing cells per column and exact duplicate rows.
insights: 'Precip Type' has 517 missing values (0.536%) - categorical; suggested fix: fill with the mode or an 'Unknown' label.
24 fully duplicated rows (0.025%) - remove with drop_duplicates().

outliers.description: Extreme values flagged with two methods: IQR fences (Q1-1.5*IQR, Q3+1.5*IQR) and Z-score (|z| > 3).
insights: Most outlier-prone feature: 'Pressure (millibars)' (3284 IQR outliers, 3.451%).
No IQR outliers in: ['Wind Bearing (degrees)', 'Visibility (km)'].

noise.description: Is there noise in the data, and how much? Each numeric feature is tested for random fluctuation and isolated spikes (= NOISE) and for stuck sensors and physically impossible readings (= DATA ERRORS), then given a verdict.

method.noise_to_signal: Robust noise sigma (MAD of the 2nd difference / sqrt(6)) divided by the feature's robust spread (MAD-based, immune to bad readings). 0 = perfectly smooth, 1 = pure random noise. Window-free, so the daily and seasonal cycles are NOT counted as noise.
method.snr_db: 10*log10(signal variance / noise variance). Above 20 dB is very clean; below 5 dB is noisy.
method.von_neumann: Mean squared step-to-step change / variance. Near 0 = smooth curve, near 2 = random.
method.spikes: A reading more than 4 robust sigmas AND more than 50% of the feature's spread away from the median of its 4 neighbours, while the neighbours agree with each other (one-point blip, not a real step change).
method.stuck_sensor: At least 24 identical consecutive readings on a continuous feature.
method.out_of_range: Values outside the physically possible range of the quantity. They are excluded from the noise tests (and from outliers, correlation, KDE and monthly analysis) and reported as data errors.

insights: Random noise: YES in 2 of 6 features: ['Wind Speed (km/h)', 'Visibility (km)'].
Data errors: YES in 2 feature(s): ['Visibility (km)', 'Pressure (millibars)'].
Noisiest: 'Wind Speed (km/h)' (noise/signal 0.33); cleanest: 'Pressure (millibars)' (0.02).
'Wind Speed (km/h)': moderate random fluctuation (noise is 33% of the signal's spread).
'Visibility (km)': moderate random fluctuation (noise is 17% of the signal's spread); 2539 isolated spikes (2.632%); stuck at 0 for 193 consecutive readings (probably a sensor outage).
'Pressure (millibars)': 1288 physically impossible values (valid range 850 to 1090).
Clean features (no action needed): ['Temperature (C)', 'Apparent Temperature (C)', 'Humidity'].
'Wind Bearing (degrees)' not tested: circular variable (0 and 360 degrees are the same direction), so linear noise tests are not meaningful.
Recommended cleaning: set impossible/stuck readings to NaN and interpolate over time. The outlier, correlation, KDE and monthly sections already ignore impossible values.
Note: wind speed fluctuates naturally (gusts), so its noise flag is expected - smooth it (rolling median / daily mean) rather than deleting points.

insights: 'Temperature (C)' averages highest in July (22.97) and lowest in January (0.82).
'Humidity' averages highest in December (0.87) and lowest in August (0.64).
Most variable month for 'Temperature (C)': 2013-04 (std 7.22).
Most variable month for 'Humidity': 2015-08 (std 0.23).

model_phase.description: Model phase: analysis of target class balance ('Precip Type'), data preprocessing using sklearn Pipeline and ColumnTransformer, and Random Forest feature importance ranking.
insights: Class balance on 'Precip Type': the dataset is SEVERELY IMBALANCED. 'rain' has 85,224 instances (88.4%), while 'snow' has 10,712 instances (11.1%), and 517 missing values (0.54%).
Imbalance ratio: approximately 7.96:1 (rain vs snow). Because of this severe skew, models trained without class weighting would suffer from majority class bias.

Preprocessing: divided dataset into 7 numerical features ['Temperature (C)', 'Apparent Temperature (C)', 'Humidity', 'Wind Speed (km/h)', 'Wind Bearing (degrees)', 'Visibility (km)', 'Pressure (millibars)'] and 1 categorical feature(s) ['Summary']. Built a ColumnTransformer combining a numerical Pipeline (median imputation + StandardScaler) and a categorical Pipeline (most-frequent imputation + OneHotEncoder).
Top predictor: 'Temperature (C)' contributes 52.7% of the decision tree splits. Combined with 'Apparent Temperature (C)' (33.6%), temperature metrics account for 86.3% of total feature importance.

Meteorological interpretation: whether precipitation falls as rain or snow is almost entirely governed by atmospheric temperature and apparent temperature around the freezing point (0°C), while humidity, pressure, and visibility provide minor secondary signals.
